text:
Unexpectedly the night lights up.

For there is another clarity for what is imagined.

What superhuman face comes on the stems

of absence to open in the night

the dream of its own essence?

What nostalgia remembers itself

and, without wishing to, murmurs its ancient

vestiges of secret happiness?

And what lips open and

—at so tender a distance—

speak of love and death

with words of childhood?

Time dissolves

and nothing is necessary anymore

once you approach, gate of paradise.

Is there night? Is there life? Are there voices?

What terror suddenly consumes us, as we look at each other?

Soul, what is your name?

translation.title: Unexpectedly
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the sudden illumination and the poem's questions around absence, childhood, paradise, and the soul's name.
